intuition: Keep a continuous window whose product is below k. Multiply in the next value, then remove values from the left until the product qualifies. Every shorter suffix of that window also qualifies because all factors are at least 1. Count those suffixes by the window's length.

Multiply the next value into product, then move left while product is at least k. Division is exact because each removed value is a factor currently in the product. Once the window is valid, every suffix ending at the same right position is also valid, since removing more factors cannot raise the product.

Count these suffixes directly as right-left+1 instead of listing them. Each subarray has exactly one right endpoint, so adding that number at every endpoint counts all valid subarrays once. The inequality is strict: equality must trigger shrinking. When k is zero or one, no nonempty product of allowed values can qualify, so return zero before entering the main loop.
This special case also avoids trying to shrink an already-empty window.

steps: For [10,5,2,6] and k=100, the first window product is 10, adding one valid subarray.
At 5, product becomes 50. Both [5] and [10,5] are valid, raising count to 3.
At 2, product reaches 100, which is not strictly below the threshold.
Remove factor 10, leaving product 10 and left=1. Add [2] and [5,2], raising count to 5.
Return count 8 without constructing any of the counted subarrays.

codeNotes.note: Every allowed nonempty product is at least one, so these thresholds have no answers.
Equality is invalid because the required comparison is strictly less than k.
All suffixes of the repaired window are valid and share this unique right endpoint.

keyDecision: The comparison is strictly product < k. For k <= 1, no nonempty window can qualify.
